versions.description: The Echo Of A Titan Long before the fracture of the outer colonies, there was Atlas—not merely a being, but a Titan whose mastery of terrestrial mapping and anomaly detection became the stuff of legend. The Titans were no ordinary civilization; their society eclipsed modern humanity in every known field—science, sorcery, and philosophy—crafting a brilliance now lost to time. When the [red moon] rose, it all turned to ash. In their final moments, Atlas stood alone, upholding the celestial sphere. Efforts to retrieve or replicate him failed. He vanished, leaving behind only scattered data, cryptic schematics, and broken relics. Refusing to let this knowledge die, the Initiative undertook a bold and secretive endeavor. Over decades of unstable prototypes and forbidden algorithms, a sentinel was born—A.T.L.A.S., the Automated Terrestrial Legacy Analysis Sentinel. Not a mere imitation, but a calculated evolution· A construct built to analyze forgotten worlds, trace the movements of vanished gods, and confront anomalies that defy understanding. It does not carry the soul of a Titan, yet something within it remembers. And it watches the stars... as if waiting for the [red moon] to rise again.

Each decade from the top of the mountain, that young and energetic girl would bring that timid but knowledgeable boy to the entrance of the hiking trail. Their footsteps shimmering as they climbed to the very top of that monolith, that quiet mountain in the distance. At the peak, where the rocky cliffs towered above all and when evil swelled to it's fullest breath, at the height of the vilest midnight, a gentle violet radiance spilled throughout the streets. The screams of agony and depression quelled. The people looked to the skies and smiled. And so the blackest night split open. A brilliance in the vantablack; Doors creaked. Windows glowed. Those med who held knives in fists full of rage and fury dropped them to wipe the tears form their faces. Women who screamed curses and whispered witchcraft looked up and wept instead. Something within the townsfolk changed on those night, for that light did not burn; it forgave. Until one decade, the girl showed alone. Up at that hiking trail, without that boy; the conduit, he did not follow. Still, she climbed, still, she peaked. But as the vilest, most demonic pitch of midnight deepened into darkness, there was no violet. The monolith remained quiet. The screams in the town did not stop. All to remain was the feeling of your skin crawling in a void, alive, aphotic and terrifying.

versions.description: It was a conduit; knowledgeable and guiding. A flicker in the marrow of an age broken for centuries. It was long ago. So long ago that the elders argue if it was memory or dream, but there was to be light. Violet and powerful. For decades it shone on the townsfolk and each time it did, they turned their ways of evil away. But that was long ago. The townsfolk did not speak of the night the violet failed; yet they felt it. In the weeks that followed, their rage did not exhaust itself. It rooted. Rooted in the grief that did not soften. It sharpened. It sharpened in the air itself for it seemed tighter, as though the world had inhaled and forgotten how to breathe out. The girl did not return. Some say she tried to climb again. Some whisper she could not bear to do it without him. They were all wrong for the monolith, it stood. It stood in silence, a place no longer of mercy but of witness. They were all wrong for on the night that has swollen with something beyond evil, a figure arrived. That conduit. And so, he climbed. His footsteps did not shimmer as they once had. they pressed into the soil like anyone else's. The forest did not hush for him this time. The wind did not turn inward. The path felt itself steeper, as though the mountain remembered his absence. as though it was screaming to him that he had been forsaken for far too long. At the peak, beneath a sky thick with unspent darkness, he did not wait for evil to swell. He let it. He let the vilest midnight reach its fullest breath. He let the town below churn with unchecked anger, with years of unpurified grief. Knives were drawn. Curses spat. Doors slammed harder than they had in decades past. But then, he pushed his face to the pitch black sky, and a light poured from the tears that left his eyes. Not violet. Blue. And it was so, so, cold.

It saw how the [[Leviathan|Great Serpent]] chose its few, and it saw how the gods above ignored the crushing truth of the deep.

The Hunter grew tired of the leftovers of divinity.

It hunted the [[Manta|drifting]] [[Bioluminescent|phosphor]] until the reefs went dim, and it drained the [[Aquaria|crystalline pulse]] from the very veins of the sea. Armed with these stolen fragments, it did not wait for the [[Leviathan|Great Serpent]] to offer a crown, nor did it bow to the [[Poseidon|King of Storms]]. It descended into the crushing weight and took what it wanted.

The Hunter is no longer a ghost in the vanta-black. It has become the ocean’s newest scar—a self-made sovereign that the abyss could not break, and that the heavens cannot command.

I can't tell whatever it's day or night, but the sky glows with an artificial light, and thick fog blankets everything. Street lamps flicker sporadically along the path, accompanied by scattered road signs. But I've never seen a car, a person, or even a single thing moving. Each time I dream, the duration seems to stretch longer. At first, it felt like less than an hour. But now... It feels like decades have passed. There seems to be nothing allowed to me but walking. Or maybe I've long since forgotten how to even try doing anything else. When I walk in this dream, I count the seconds. 2,207,568,830... I think it's been over seventy years. Please, someone get me out of here. Where is this? Free me. What is happening to me? Let me out. Who am I? Help me please... Maybe death would be better than this...

Thus, Sol bestowed consciousness upon his weapons, leaving them behind as his legacy—so that even after his disappearance, they would continue the eternal hunt for chaos. Now, it stands as Sol's final legacy—and the only key to the tomb where he rests. For countless ages, the sword has continued its search, seeking both the shattered remnants of its kin and the dormant seeds of chaos.

When Poseidon rose, the sea bent to his will—all but one. Leviathan—a god not born, but formed by the crushing weight of the deep, crowned by silence, and veiled in time.

As time went on, a hunter came—merciless, tireless—tearing through the deep, leaving only silence in its path. But even it, for all its hunger, veered away from the deepest trench. It knows. All things do. Leviathan is not prey. It is not predator. It is the ocean's oldest wound—still open, still waiting.

No records speak its name. No temple dares. It is not remembered in words, only in fear. And it is said: to say its name is to awaken it.

And when it awakens, it does not rage blindly. It chooses—not many, only a rare few. To them, it does what not many gods of Olympus ever could: it crowns them. Not with gold or laurel, but with the weight of the abyss. Kings not of men, but something deeper.

Through them, it stirs. Through them, it remembers.

It changes them.

Their vision pierces deeper than darkness. Their fear is drowned. Their will is no longer their own. What returns from its touch no longer human, no longer whole. They are made to endure, made to rule.

Since then, the sea has not known peace—only waiting.

versions.description: Do you remember those summers? I do... though each year, the memories become a little blurrier. I still hear the laughter carried by the evening breeze, echoing between rows of glowing lanterns that seemed to stretch into the stars. The air was warm, sweet with the scent of food from stalls I'd race between without a single worry in my mind. Back then, time didn't matter. Tomorrow always felt infinitely for away. I thought those nights would never end. I chased fireflies until the sky turned black, watched fireworks bloom like flowers above my head, and believed every wish I whispered into the summer wind would somehow come true. The world felt so much bigger then... yet somehow safer. Simpler. Funny, isn't it? The festival still returns every year. The lanterns still sway. The music still plays. Children still laugh exactly as we once did. Yet when I walk those same paths now, something is missing. Maybe it isn't the festival that's changed. Maybe it's me. The days became shorter. Responsibilities replaced wonder. Somewhere along the way, I stopped looking up when the fireworks painted the sky. I stopped chasing moments because I was too busy chasing tomorrow. *If I could go back... even for one more evening... I'd run through those streets again without thinking about time. I'd hold onto those fleeting moments just a little longer. I'd tell my younger self not to grow up so quickly. Because I finally understand... The most precious memories are the ones you never realize you're making. So if you ever find yourself beneath the glow of summer lanterns, with music dancing through the night and laughter all around you... Stay a little longer. For someone, somewhere... They're already missing this moment.

versions.description: A young girl once received a strange piece of Quartz for her birthday from her mother, said to be able to grow into a beautiful flower. From there on, she made it her mission to, one day, see the flower bloom. She would water it every time its soil ran dry, and she would cut away the leaves of the garden's trees whenever they threatened to drown out the sun for the little flower. Soon enough, the Quartz would indeed transform into a strong and healthy young Rose, with petals coloured in the brightest pink the girl had ever seen. Yet, despite her best attempts and all her loving care... ...the Rose would not bloom. Still, the girl was determined to one day see it spread its petals, and so she would continue taking care of it. Until one day, when her mother grew incredibly ill. The girl did not know what to do, take care of her beloved mother, or the rose she wanted so dearly to see bloom. Alas, the choice was her mother, forcing the girl to abandon the Rose in the garden. After a few days, however, her mother felt the end approaching, so she motioned her dear daughter to come closer, and whispered into ear: "Give it your entire heart, like how I've given mine to you." The girl understood and tears began to fall from her face as her mother drew her last breath. Thus, she returned to the garden one more time, the Rose's petals already wilting. It looked hopeless, but just when the girl's tears fell onto the soil, the Rose's petals spread wide open, and a magnificent, pink light, shaped like a heart, illuminated the garden for 3 days and 7 nights. Then, the girl understood: "No matter how hopeless it seems, no matter how much you've lost. Keep moving forward."

The eyes of children climb upward in hopes of catching a glimpse of the revered Sky Festival in the briefest moments it dips below the clouds. The Sky festival annually sails the globe to distribute all kinds of sweet treats to those young and old, under only the condition that they believe. Lest they not, the ship remains invisible. The ship is silent as it soars, needing not to make a crescendo upon its arrival; the rain of goods that follows it is more than sufficient. It is unknown how it constantly generates such large mounds of sweets—assumably driven by the same great force that allows the Sky Festival to fly in the first place—believing. It is gone as fast as it comes, a one day global trip, only touching water once it reaches the shorelines of Easter Island, and where it ends up upon touchdown? A forever remaining secret.

versions.description: Think of a god that never finished being made. Not glowing with anything holy, just buzzing with this unease you can't quite place, like a signal that never fully tunes in. It drifts and it has no say in that. No hunger, no fear, no direction it chose. It occupies a body the way a guest occupies a room they weren't invited into, present but not quite in possession of anything. And the way it comes into being is the cruelest part. It loops. You don't arrive somewhere new, you just resurface in the same place you left, holding time that doesn't belong to the moment you woke up in. Stuck in an era that kept moving without you. The universe is so precise it almost feels personal, everything slotting into place with this quiet confidence. And then there's this. Sitting inside all that order like a word written in the wrong language. Not broken, not dangerous, just fundamentally out of place in a way that nobody around it seems to notice or care about. Nothing moves through it by its own choosing. It doesn't get to feel its own existence from the inside. It just persists in a body, in a timeline, in a life that keeps happening whether it's ready or not, whether it's even there or not. End log.
